mainTopic: סמיכה (who may give it, where, and to whom, with stories about it), and the number of judges for עריפת עגלה.
overview: The amud opens by finishing רב's statement that without רבי יהודה בן בבא, the laws of קנסות would have disappeared. Rome had outlawed סמיכה. רבי יהודה בן בבא ordained five or six great students in a deserted spot, and he was killed for it. The גמרא rejects the idea that this proves one sage alone can ordain, because others may have been with him. It also explains that רבי מאיר was ordained twice, because the people had not accepted רבי עקיבא's סמיכה. Next, רבי יהושע בן לוי teaches that there is no סמיכה outside ארץ ישראל: the act of ordaining, and even the candidate, must be in the Land. Then come stories: why the house of עלי is not ordained, how רבי זירא hid from סמיכה, and the songs sung to honor great חכמים. Finally the גמרא returns to the משנה's rule on עריפת עגלה, where רבי יהודה requires five judges and רבי שמעון three. It explains how each reads the פסוק, and the ברייתא about the plural verbs continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Rome outlaws סמיכה
steps.stepSummary: The story explains why the laws of קנסות almost ended: Rome made a deadly decree against anyone who gave or received סמיכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The laws of fines would have ended among the Jewish people. Once, the wicked Roman kingdom decreed persecution against the Jews: whoever ordains will be killed, whoever is ordained will be killed, the city where ordination happens will be destroyed, and the boundary areas where they ordain will be uprooted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues רב's story by describing the Roman decree that threatened to wipe out סמיכה. This sets up the story of what רבי יהודה בן בבא did about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only judges with סמיכה can rule on דיני קנסות. If no one could give or receive סמיכה, the chain would break and these laws could no longer be judged. Rome also punished whole cities so that people would be afraid to let ordination happen near them.

keyTerms.meaning: Cases of fines fixed by the תורה, which only judges with סמיכה can rule on
The one who gives סמיכה (ordination) and the one who receives it
Boundary areas around a city (תחומי שבת)

steps.whyThisMatters: The danger explains why רבי יהודה בן בבא may have acted alone. That is the point the גמרא wants to use as a proof.

phrases.english: the laws of fines would have ceased from the Jewish people,
because once the wicked kingdom decreed
religious persecution against the Jewish people:
that anyone who ordains will be killed,
and anyone who is ordained will be killed,
and a city in which they ordain will be destroyed,
and boundary areas in which they ordain will be uprooted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רב's statement that began just before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Rome decreed death for anyone giving or receiving סמיכה, and destruction for the place where it happened.

steps.title: רבי יהודה בן בבא ordains the elders alone
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה בן בבא goes to a deserted spot between אושא and שפרעם and ordains five elders. רב אויא counts a sixth. The story names only him as the one who ordained.
steps.simpleTranslation: What did יהודה בן בבא do? He went and sat between two large mountains, between two large cities, between two תחומי שבת, between אושא and שפרעם. There he ordained five elders: רבי מאיר, רבי יהודה, רבי שמעון, רבי יוסי, and רבי אלעזר בן שמוע. רב אויא adds: also רבי נחמיה.
steps.whatsHappening: The story tells what רבי יהודה בן בבא did. Because only he is mentioned as ordaining, this looks like proof that one sage alone can give סמיכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He picked a spot that belonged to no city and no city's boundary, so no town would be destroyed because of him. The story names only one person doing the ordaining, which is the basis of the proof. רב אויא adds רבי נחמיה to the list.

keyTerms.meaning: Elders; here, the sages who received סמיכה
The area around a town where one may walk on שבת

phrases.english: What did Yehuda ben Bava do?
He went and sat himself down
between two large mountains,
and between two large cities,
and between two Shabbat boundaries,
between Usha and Shefaram,
and there he ordained five elders.

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵלּוּ הֵן: רַבִּי מֵאִיר, וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה,
phrases.english: And these are they: Rabbi Meir, and Rabbi Yehuda,
and Rabbi Shimon, and Rabbi Yosei,
and Rabbi Elazar ben Shammua.

phrases.aramaic: רַב אַוְיָא מוֹסִיף: אַף רַבִּי נְחֶמְיָה.
phrases.english: Rav Avya adds: also Rabbi Nechemya.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tells his response to the decree described in step 1.
steps.raayaObject: That סמיכה can be given by one sage alone.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story names only רבי יהודה בן בבא as the one who ordained the elders.

steps.title: רבי יהודה בן בבא dies as a martyr
steps.stepSummary: The enemies find them. He tells his students to run, refuses to let them stay for him, and is killed with three hundred iron spears.
steps.simpleTranslation: When their enemies found them, he said: My sons, run! They said: רבי, what will happen to you? He said: I am lying before them like a stone that no one can turn over. People say the soldiers did not leave until they had stuck three hundred iron spears into him and made him like a sieve.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends with רבי יהודה בן בבא saving his students and giving up his own life. This finishes the story before the גמרא goes back to checking the proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He was old and could not escape, so he told the young sages to save themselves. If they had stayed to help him, they would all have died. This shows the price he paid to keep סמיכה going.

keyTerms.meaning: A stone no one turns over, meaning he could not be moved or saved

phrases.english: Once their enemies discovered them,
he said to them: My sons, run!

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: רַבִּי, מָה תְּהֵא עָלֶיךָ?
phrases.english: They said to him: Rebbi, what will become of you?
He said to them: I am lying before them
like a stone that no one turns over.
phrases.notes: He means he is too old to get away. Staying to help him would not save him.

phrases.english: People say: they did not move from there
until they had stuck into him three hundred
spears of iron
and made him like a sieve.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the story begun in steps 1 and 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה בן בבא gave his life so that סמיכה would not end.

steps.title: Maybe others ordained together with him
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof: other sages may have joined him but were left unnamed out of respect for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Other sages were with רבי יהודה בן בבא. The reason the story does not count them is out of respect for רבי יהודה בן בבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof from the story. The fact that only one person is named does not show that only one person ordained.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof depended on the story mentioning only one ordaining sage. The גמרא says there could have been others there to make up the required three. They were left out because he was the greatest and gave his life, so the story honors him alone.
steps.confusionAlert: The story is not being called untrue. The גמרא only says it does not prove that one person alone can ordain.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בָּבָא אַחֲרִינֵי הֲווֹ בַּהֲדֵיהּ,
phrases.english: With Rabbi Yehuda ben Bava, there were others with him,
and the fact that it does not list them

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם כְּבוֹדוֹ דְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בָּבָא.
phrases.english: is because of the honor of Rabbi Yehuda ben Bava.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בָּבָא אַחֲרִינֵי הֲווֹ בַּהֲדֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof drawn from step 2.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof that one sage can ordain. The story itself stands.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Leaving others unnamed does not mean they were not there. They may have been left out to honor him.
steps.whatToRemember: The story of רבי יהודה בן בבא does not prove that one person can give סמיכה, because others may have been with him.

steps.title: Wasn't רבי מאיר ordained by רבי עקיבא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבי יהודה בן בבא could have ordained רבי מאיר, since רבי יוחנן says that רבי עקיבא ordained him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did רבי יהודה בן בבא really ordain רבי מאיר? But רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: Anyone who says רבי עקיבא did not ordain רבי מאיר is simply mistaken!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new difficulty with the story. Its list of who was ordained clashes with a known teaching about רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן strongly says that רבי עקיבא ordained רבי מאיר. If so, why would רבי יהודה בן בבא need to ordain him again? The challenge targets the story's list of names, not the question of how many sages are needed.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't [so-and-so] say? (a challenge from a known teaching)

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי מֵאִיר, רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בָּבָא סַמְכֵיהּ?
phrases.english: And Rabbi Meir: did Rabbi Yehuda ben Bava ordain him?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה
phrases.english: But didn't Rabba bar bar Chana say
that Rabbi Yochanan said:
Anyone who says that Rabbi Meir
was not ordained by Rabbi Akiva
is nothing but mistaken!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי מֵאִיר, רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בָּבָא סַמְכֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question about a detail in the step 2 story.
steps.kashyaTarget: The story's claim that רבי יהודה בן בבא ordained רבי מאיר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן says רבי עקיבא ordained רבי מאיר, so a second סמיכה seems pointless.

steps.title: Ordained twice: the second time was accepted
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא did ordain רבי מאיר, but the people did not accept it. When רבי יהודה בן בבא ordained him later, they did.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא ordained him, but they did not accept it. רבי יהודה בן בבא ordained him, and they accepted it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by saying both reports are true. There were two סמיכות, and only the second was accepted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן is right that רבי עקיבא gave רבי מאיר סמיכה, but the people did not accept it then. So רבי יהודה בן בבא ordained him again, and this time it was accepted. That is why he appears in the story's list.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר received סמיכה twice: first from רבי עקיבא, which was not accepted, and later from רבי יהודה בן בבא, which was.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva ordained him, but they did not accept it;
phrases.notes: "They" means the people. They did not go along with the appointment.

phrases.aramaic: סְמָכֶיהָ רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בָּבָא וְקַיבְּלוּהּ.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda ben Bava ordained him, and they accepted it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Both reports are true and refer to two different events.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The challenge assumed a sage is ordained only once, so the two reports seemed to contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי עקיבא's סמיכה was not accepted, so רבי יהודה בן בבא ordained רבי מאיר again, and that one was accepted.

steps.title: No ordination outside the Land of Israel
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי rules that there is no סמיכה outside ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי said: There is no ordination outside the Land of Israel.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new rule from רבי יהושע בן לוי: סמיכה does not happen outside ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier steps were about who did the ordaining. Now the topic shifts to where סמיכה can happen. The wording is short, so the גמרא will next ask what exactly it means.

keyTerms.meaning: Ordination of a judge, which gives him the full authority of the chain going back to משה

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
There is no ordination outside the Land [of Israel].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the story of רבי יהודה בן בבא's ordinations to a new rule about where סמיכה can take place.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: סמיכה does not take place outside ארץ ישראל.

steps.title: What does 'no ordination' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבי יהושע בן לוי means by 'there is no סמיכה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'there is no ordination' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the rule really means. This sets up the next two moves, a first guess and then a better answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'No סמיכה' could mean two things. It could mean ordained judges have no power to act outside the Land. Or it could mean the act of ordaining cannot be done there.

keyTerms.meaning: What? (asks for the meaning of something)

phrases.english: What does "there is no ordination" mean?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of the rule just stated.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether 'no סמיכה' means no judging of fine cases outside the Land, or no act of ordaining outside the Land.

steps.title: First guess rejected: a Sanhedrin works outside the Land too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the rule means דיני קנסות are not judged outside the Land. It rejects this using a משנה that says a סנהדרין functions everywhere.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it means that they do not judge cases of fines at all outside the Land, that is a problem. Didn't we learn in a משנה: A סנהדרין functions both in the Land and outside the Land?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries one meaning: ordained judges cannot judge cases of fines outside the Land. It shoots this down at once with a משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Cases of fines need ordained judges. If such judges could not judge outside the Land, a סנהדרין could not work there. But the משנה says a סנהדרין does work outside the Land, so this meaning cannot be right.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (introduces a guess that will be rejected)
Cases of fines, which only ordained judges may judge
But didn't we learn (in a משנה)?

phrases.english: If you say that they do not judge
cases of fines at all outside the Land,
but didn't we learn in a Mishnah:
A Sanhedrin functions
both in the Land and outside the Land!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵּימָא דְּלָא דָּיְינִי דִּינֵי קְנָסוֹת כְּלָל בְּחוּצָה לָאָרֶץ וְהָא תְּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a first answer to the question and immediately challenges it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that ordained judges cannot judge cases of fines outside the Land.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה says a סנהדרין functions outside the Land, so ordained judges must be able to judge there.

steps.title: Real meaning: we do not ordain outside the Land
steps.stepSummary: The rule means that the act of ordaining cannot be done outside ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it means that we do not ordain judges outside the Land.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the correct meaning. Judges who are already ordained can judge anywhere, but the ordaining itself must happen in ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This keeps the משנה about the סנהדרין intact. The limit is on the act of סמיכה, not on the power of a judge who is already ordained.
steps.whatToRemember: Ordained judges can judge outside the Land. Only the act of ordaining must happen in ארץ ישראל.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up 'ordaining' with 'judging.' Outside the Land you cannot make new judges, but judges ordained in the Land still have their power there.

phrases.english: Rather, it means that we do not ordain outside the Land.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected first guess with the correct meaning.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'No סמיכה' means ordained judges have no power outside the Land.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'No סמיכה' means the act of ordaining cannot happen outside the Land.

steps.title: What if only the candidate is outside the Land?
steps.stepSummary: If the ordaining rabbis are outside the Land, it clearly does not work. The גמרא asks about the reverse: the rabbis are in the Land and the candidate is outside.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is obvious that if those ordaining are outside the Land and those being ordained are in the Land, we already said it does not work. But if those ordaining are in the Land and those being ordained are outside the Land, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets aside the obvious case and asks about the split case. Can rabbis in ארץ ישראל ordain someone who is outside the Land?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Rabbis ordaining outside the Land is exactly what the rule forbids. The open question is whether it is enough for the ordaining rabbis to be in the Land. Or does the candidate also need to be there?

phrases.english: It is obvious:
if those ordaining are outside the Land and those being ordained are in the Land,
we already said that it does not work.
But if those ordaining are in the Land
and those being ordained are outside the Land, what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּשִׁיטָא סוֹמְכִין בְּחוּצָה לָאָרֶץ וְנִסְמָכִין בָּאָרֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the meaning just set and asks how far it reaches.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether rabbis in ארץ ישראל may ordain someone who is outside the Land.

steps.title: Proof: those not present in the Land were not ordained
steps.stepSummary: Stories show that people who were not with the rabbis in ארץ ישראל were not ordained. So the candidate must also be in the Land.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבי יוחנן was distressed about רב שמן בר אבא, because he was not with them so that he could ordain him. Also, רבי שמעון בן זירוד and one who was with him, namely רבי יונתן בן עכמאי (and some say the reverse): the one who was with them was ordained, and the one who was not with them was not ordained.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with stories. In each one, a worthy scholar was not ordained only because he was not there in ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If ordaining from a distance worked, רבי יוחנן would have had nothing to be upset about. He could simply have ordained רב שמן בר אבא from afar. Also, of two equal scholars, only the one who was present was ordained. So the candidate must be in the Land.
steps.whatToRemember: For סמיכה, both the ordaining rabbis and the candidate must be in ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
that Rabbi Yochanan was distressed
about Rav Shemen bar Abba,
because he was not with them so that he could ordain him.
phrases.notes: 'With them' means with the rabbis in ארץ ישראל at the time of the ordaining.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן זֵירוּד וְחַד דְּעִימֵּיהּ,
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Zeirud and one who was with him,
And who is he? Rabbi Yonatan ben Akhmai.
And some say:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן בֶּן עַכְמַאי וְחַד דְּעִימֵּיהּ,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yonatan ben Akhmai and one who was with him,
And who is he? Rabbi Shimon ben Zeirud.
The one who was with them, they ordained,

phrases.aramaic: וְחַד דְּלָא הֲוָה גַּבַּיְיהוּ – לָא סַמְכוּהּו.
phrases.english: and the one who was not with them, they did not ordain.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן הֲוָה מִצְטַעֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 11 using stories of actual practice.
steps.raayaObject: That a candidate outside ארץ ישראל cannot be ordained, even by rabbis in the Land.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן's distress over רב שמן בר אבא, and the case of רבי שמעון בן זירוד and רבי יונתן בן עכמאי, where only the one present was ordained.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's failed attempts to ordain רבי חנינא and רבי הושעיא
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן kept trying to ordain רבי חנינא and רבי הושעיא but it never worked out. They comforted him, saying they came from the house of עלי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן was eagerly trying to ordain רבי חנינא and רבי הושעיא. It did not work out, and he was very upset. They said to him: Let the master not be upset, for we come from the house of עלי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells another story about סמיכה. This time the problem is not where the candidates were. Things kept getting in the way, and the two rabbis told רבי יוחנן not to be upset because of their family line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a story, not a proof for the earlier question. The two rabbis explain the failure by their family: they come from עלי the כהן גדול. That family was cursed, so they took it as expected that they would not reach this honor.

keyTerms.meaning: Was eagerly trying, worked hard at
The matter did not work out
The family of עלי the כהן גדול

phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina and Rabbi Hoshaya:

phrases.aramaic: הֲוָה קָא מִשְׁתְּקִיד רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לְמִיסְמְכִינְהוּ.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan was eagerly trying to ordain them.
The matter did not work out,
and he was very distressed.
They said to him: Let the master not be distressed,
for we come from the house of Eli.
phrases.notes: They are hinting at the curse on עלי's family in שמואל א 2:31-33.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי חֲנִינָא וְרַבִּי הוֹשַׁעְיָא הֲוָה קָא מִשְׁתְּקִיד רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לְמִיסְמְכִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of רבי יוחנן's distress over ordinations, now with a story whose reason is not location.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Not a ruling: a story in which the failure to ordain is blamed on the candidates' descent from the house of עלי.

steps.title: The source that the house of Eli is not ordained
steps.stepSummary: רבי יונתן brings a פסוק showing that descendants of עלי do not receive סמיכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי שמואל בר נחמן said in the name of רבי יונתן: How do we know that people from the house of עלי are not ordained? Because the פסוק says, 'There will not be a זקן in your house all the days.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up the comfort from step 13 by showing where the idea that עלי's family is not ordained comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 13, רבי חנינא and רבי הושעיא said they could not be ordained because they come from the house of עלי. Here the גמרא gives the source: a פסוק cursing עלי's family that there will be no 'זקן' in his house. The next steps explain why 'זקן' must mean an ordained sage.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know? (asking for a source)
the family and descendants of עלי the כהן גדול
elder; can mean an old man or an ordained sage

phrases.english: As Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachman said
that Rabbi Yonatan said:
From where do we know that people from the house of Eli are not ordained?

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״לֹא יִהְיֶה זָקֵן בְּבֵיתְךָ כׇּל הַיָּמִים״.
phrases.english: As it says: "There will not be an elder in your house all the days."

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source behind the comfort offered to רבי יוחנן in step 13.
steps.raayaObject: That descendants of עלי cannot receive סמיכה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The פסוק 'לא יהיה זקן בביתך כל הימים' (שמואל א 2:32).

steps.title: Elder cannot mean an old man
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what 'זקן' means and shows it cannot mean a literally old man, since another פסוק already says they will die young.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'זקן' mean? If you say it means a truly old person, but another פסוק already says, 'All the increase of your house will die as young men'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the meaning of the word 'זקן' and rules out the simple meaning of 'old man.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The very next פסוק already says that עלי's descendants will die young. If 'זקן' just meant 'old man,' the first פסוק would be saying the same thing twice. So 'זקן' must mean something else.

phrases.english: What is meant by "elder"?
If you say it means an actual old person,
but isn't it written: "All those raised in your house will die as young men"!
phrases.notes: שמואל א 2:33. Dying as young men already means they won't reach old age, so the first פסוק must mean something new.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי זָקֵן? אִילֵּימָא זָקֵן מַמָּשׁ, וְהָכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the meaning of the key word in the פסוק from step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading 'זקן' in the פסוק as a literally old man.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The next פסוק already says they will die young, so reading 'זקן' as 'old man' would make the first פסוק repeat the same thing.

steps.title: Elder means ordination
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that 'זקן' refers to סמיכה, the title of an ordained sage.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it means סמיכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question: 'זקן' in the פסוק means an ordained sage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since 'old man' doesn't work, 'זקן' is read as the title of an ordained חכם. So the curse means no one from עלי's family will receive סמיכה. This confirms the comfort given to רבי יוחנן in step 13.
steps.whatToRemember: The descendants of עלי cannot receive סמיכה, because 'there will be no זקן in your house' means no ordained sage.

phrases.english: Rather, it means ordination.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the problem raised in step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting a word in the פסוק
steps.terutzMaskana: 'זקן' means an ordained sage, so the house of עלי receives no סמיכה.

steps.title: רבי זירא hides to avoid ordination
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא used to hide so he would not be ordained, because רבי אלעזר taught that staying unknown leads to a long life.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא used to hide so they would not ordain him, because רבי אלעזר said: Always stay in the background and you will live.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new story about סמיכה: רבי זירא tried to avoid being ordained.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זירא was not avoiding סמיכה because he was unworthy. He followed רבי אלעזר's teaching that staying humble and unknown brings long life, while a public position can shorten it.

keyTerms.meaning: obscure and alive (stay unknown and live long)

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira would hide so they would not ordain him,
because Rabbi Elazar said:
Always be obscure and stay alive.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from who cannot be ordained to a story of someone who avoided ordination.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Staying unknown leads to long life, so רבי זירא avoided סמיכה.

steps.title: רבי זירא changes his mind
steps.stepSummary: After hearing that rising to greatness brings forgiveness of all sins, רבי זירא presented himself to be ordained.
steps.simpleTranslation: Once he heard what רבי אלעזר also said, that a person only rises to greatness if all his sins are forgiven, he made himself available.
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues: a second teaching of רבי אלעזר made רבי זירא stop hiding.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first teaching showed a downside to greatness, which is a shorter life. The second showed a big upside: becoming a leader comes with forgiveness of all sins. That benefit convinced רבי זירא to accept סמיכה.

keyTerms.meaning: he presented himself, made himself available

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן דְּשַׁמְעַהּ לְהָא דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר,
phrases.english: Once he heard this that Rabbi Elazar said,
a person does not rise to greatness

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן מוֹחֲלִין לוֹ עַל כׇּל עֲוֹנוֹתָיו,
phrases.english: unless all his sins are forgiven,
he presented himself.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיוָן דְּשַׁמְעַהּ לְהָא דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the רבי זירא story by explaining why he stopped hiding.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Rising to greatness brings forgiveness of all sins, so רבי זירא accepted סמיכה.

steps.title: The song sung at רבי זירא's ordination
steps.stepSummary: At רבי זירא's סמיכה they sang a bride's song: no makeup, yet full of grace.
steps.simpleTranslation: When they ordained רבי זירא, they sang to him: 'No eye shadow, no rouge, no hair dye, and yet full of grace.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells what the חכמים sang when רבי זירא was finally ordained.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This was a wedding song praising a bride whose beauty needs no makeup. Applied to רבי זירא, it means his greatness was plain to see without any outside decoration.

keyTerms.meaning: a graceful one, full of charm

phrases.english: When they ordained Rabbi Zeira,
they sang to him like this:
"No eye shadow, no rouge, and no hair dye,
and yet she is full of grace."

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי סַמְכוּהּ לְרַבִּי זֵירָא, שָׁרוּ לֵיהּ הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the רבי זירא story with what happened at his ordination.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי זירא's worthiness was obvious without any outside 'decoration.'

steps.title: The song at the ordination of רבי אמי and רבי אסי
steps.stepSummary: At the סמיכה of רבי אמי and רבי אסי they sang: ordain more like these, not unworthy people. Another version names the unworthy differently.
steps.simpleTranslation: When they ordained רבי אמי and רבי אסי, they sang: 'Anyone like these, anyone like these, ordain for us! Don't ordain for us any of the rags or the distorters.' Some say it was: 'not the robbers and not the tramplers.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second ordination song, this time for רבי אמי and רבי אסי, along with another version of its words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The song holds them up as the model of who deserves סמיכה. It also warns against ordaining unworthy people. The two versions differ only in how they describe the unworthy.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי סַמְכוּהּ לְרַבִּי אַמֵּי וּלְרַבִּי אַסִּי,
phrases.english: When they ordained Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Asi,
they sang to them like this:

phrases.aramaic: ״כֹּל מִן דֵּין, כֹּל מִן דֵּין, סְמוּכוּ לַנָא.
phrases.english: "Anyone like these, anyone like these, ordain for us.
Do not ordain for us
any of the rags or the distorters."
phrases.notes: These are insulting words for unworthy people who twist the law.

phrases.english: And some say it as:
"Not from the robbers and not from the tramplers."

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי סַמְכוּהּ לְרַבִּי אַמֵּי וּלְרַבִּי אַסִּי, שָׁרוּ לְהוּ הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second example of a song sung at an ordination.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only people like רבי אמי and רבי אסי should be ordained, not unworthy or corrupt people.

steps.title: The greeting sung to רבי אבהו
steps.stepSummary: When רבי אבהו came from the ישיבה to the Caesar's house, the ladies there sang his praises.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבי אבהו would come from the ישיבה to the Caesar's house, the noble ladies of the Caesar's house would come out and sing to him: 'Great one of his people, leader of his nation, shining lamp, may your coming be blessed with peace.'
steps.whatsHappening: Since the גמרא has been listing songs sung to חכמים, it adds one more: the greeting sung to רבי אבהו at the Caesar's court.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not about סמיכה itself. It joins the list of songs of praise because of its theme. It shows that even the non-Jewish royal household honored רבי אבהו.

keyTerms.meaning: the house of the Caesar, the Roman ruler's court

steps.whatToRemember: The section ends with songs of praise for great חכמים: רבי זירא, רבי אמי and רבי אסי at their סמיכה, and רבי אבהו at the Caesar's court.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu, when he would come
from the yeshiva to the house of the emperor,
the ladies of the emperor's house would go out
and sing to him:
"Great one of his people, leader of his nation,
lamp of light, blessed be your coming in peace."

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ, כִּי הֲוָה אָתֵי מִמְּתִיבְתָּא לְבֵי קֵיסָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a related story about a song of praise for a חכם.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אבהו was greatly honored, even by the ladies of the Caesar's court.

steps.title: The heifer case and רבי יהודה's count of five
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule about עריפת עגלה and brings a ברייתא where רבי יהודה reads the פסוק as requiring five judges.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said the breaking of the heifer's neck is done with three judges. A ברייתא teaches: the פסוק says 'And your elders and your judges shall go out.' 'Your elders' means two, and 'your judges' means two more. A court cannot have an even number, so we add one more, which makes five. This is רבי יהודה's opinion.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה, עריפת עגלה, and brings a ברייתא showing how רבי יהודה gets the number five from the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each plural word in the פסוק counts as at least two people. רבי יהודה counts both 'elders' and 'judges', which gives four. Since a court may not be evenly split, one more judge is added, so the total is five.

keyTerms.meaning: Breaking the neck of a young cow when a murdered person is found and nobody knows who killed him
An evenly balanced court, one with an even number of judges

steps.confusionAlert: Each plural word counts as only two judges, the smallest plural. The extra judge is not taken from the פסוק. It is added only so the court will not have an even number.

phrases.english: The breaking of the heifer's neck is with three.
phrases.notes: This is a quote from the משנה. רבי יהודה there says five.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
"And your elders and your judges shall go out."
"Your elders": two,
"your judges": two,
and a court may not be evenly balanced,
so we add one more to them;
so here there are five.
These are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the stories about סמיכה and returns to the משנה's list of cases.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה: עריפת עגלה needs five judges (two plus two, plus one so the court is not even).

steps.title: רבי שמעון's count of three
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון counts only 'your elders' as two, adds one, and gets three judges.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: 'Your elders' means two. A court cannot be even, so we add one more, which makes three.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון gives a different count. He uses only the word 'elders' for the number, so he gets three judges, the same as the first opinion in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון does not count 'your judges' toward the number. That leaves a question for him: what does the word 'your judges' teach? The גמרא asks this next.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
"Your elders": two,
and a court may not be evenly balanced,
so we add one more to them;
so here there are three.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing reading of the same פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי שמעון: three judges, because only 'your elders' is counted.

steps.title: What does רבי שמעון do with 'your judges'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבי שמעון learns from the word 'your judges', since he does not use it for the count.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי שמעון, what does he do with this word 'your judges'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question. Every word in the תורה must teach something, so what does 'your judges' teach for רבי שמעון?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה uses 'your judges' to add two more judges. רבי שמעון does not, so the word looks extra for him. The גמרא wants to know what he learns from it.

keyTerms.meaning: What does he do with it? (What does he learn from this word?)

phrases.english: And Rabbi Shimon,
this "your judges", what does he do with it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, הַאי ״שֹׁפְטֶיךָ״ מַאי עָבֵיד לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the word that רבי שמעון left out of his count.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What רבי שמעון learns from 'your judges'.

steps.title: 'Your judges' means the special judges
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון uses 'your judges' to teach that these judges must be the special ones, members of the סנהדרין.
steps.simpleTranslation: He needs that word to teach that they must be the special ones among your judges.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that for רבי שמעון, 'your judges' teaches what kind of judges are needed, not how many.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The judges for עגלה ערופה cannot be just any judges. They must be the top judges of the nation, the סנהדרין. For רבי שמעון, the word 'your judges' teaches this.

keyTerms.meaning: He needs it (to teach something else)
The special, outstanding ones (here, members of the סנהדרין)

phrases.english: He needs that
for the special ones among your judges.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'Your judges' teaches that the judges must be from the סנהדרין.

steps.title: Where does רבי יהודה learn this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where רבי יהודה learns that the judges must be special, since he uses 'your judges' for the count.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהודה? Where does he learn this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the question around. רבי יהודה used 'your judges' for the number, so how does he know the judges must be from the סנהדרין?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree that the judges must be special. רבי יהודה used up 'your judges' on the count, so he needs a different source for this.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda?
phrases.notes: He's asking where רבי יהודה learns that they must be the special judges.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks the same kind of question about the other opinion.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: רבי יהודה's source that the judges must be from the סנהדרין.

steps.title: From 'your elders' instead of 'elders'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה learns it from the extra word 'your': the פסוק says 'your elders' and not just 'elders'.
steps.simpleTranslation: He learns it from the fact that the פסוק says 'your elders' instead of just 'elders'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי יהודה finds the source in the word 'your'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just 'elders' could mean any old or respected people. 'Your elders' means the special elders of the whole nation, the סנהדרין. So רבי יהודה does not need the word 'judges' for this.

keyTerms.meaning: It comes out from, it is learned from

phrases.english: From "elders" becoming "your elders" it comes out.
phrases.notes: The פסוק could have said just 'elders'. Adding 'your' points to the elders who belong to the whole nation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 26.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'Your elders' (and not just 'elders') teaches that they must be from the סנהדרין.

steps.title: Why רבי שמעון needs both words
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון explains that 'your elders' alone would only rule out ordinary people. 'And your judges' is needed to show they must be from the Great סנהדרין and not a small one.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי שמעון? If the פסוק said only 'elders', I would think it means elders of the marketplace, so the תורה wrote 'your elders'. And if only 'your elders' were written, I would think it means a small סנהדרין, so the תורה wrote 'and your judges', meaning the special ones among your judges.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבי שמעון does not accept that 'your elders' is enough. Each word rules out a different mistake.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are three levels. 'Elders' alone could mean any respected people in the street. 'Your elders' means real judges, but maybe only a local court of twenty-three, a סנהדרין קטנה. 'And your judges' raises it to the very top judges, the Great סנהדרין.

keyTerms.meaning: I would have thought (a mistaken first idea)
Elders of the marketplace: respected people who are not judges
A small סנהדרין, a local court of twenty-three

phrases.english: And Rabbi Shimon:
if it were from "elders",
I would have said elders of the marketplace;
so the Merciful One wrote "your elders".
And if only "your elders" were written,
I would have said a small Sanhedrin;
so the Merciful One wrote "and your judges":
from the special ones among your judges.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן: אִי מִ״זִּקְנֵי״ הֲוָה אָמֵינָא זִקְנֵי הַשּׁוּק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why רבי שמעון does not accept רבי יהודה's idea that 'your elders' alone is enough.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'Your elders' rules out ordinary people, and 'and your judges' rules out a small סנהדרין.

steps.title: רבי יהודה learns it from a גזירה שוה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה learns that they must be the Great סנהדרין from a גזירה שוה with 'the elders of the congregation' in ויקרא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהודה learns 'elders' from 'elders' in the פסוק 'And the elders of the congregation shall lay their hands'. Just as there it means the special ones of the congregation, so too here it means the special ones among your elders.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how רבי יהודה answers רבי שמעון's point. He knows they must be the top judges from a word-match with another פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'elders' also appears with the bull brought when the whole nation sins, and there it means the Great סנהדרין. A גזירה שוה connects the two places, so 'elders' here also means the Great סנהדרין. That leaves 'your judges' free for the count.

keyTerms.meaning: Just as there, so too here (the pattern of a גזירה שוה)

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda learns
"elders" from "elders"
from "And the elders of the congregation shall lay their hands":
just as there it means the special ones of the congregation,
so too here, the special ones among your elders.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבי יהודה's answer to רבי שמעון's argument.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזירה שוה from 'the elders of the congregation' shows they must be the Great סנהדרין.

steps.title: Then learn everything from there
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יהודה: if he uses the גזירה שוה, he could learn everything from it, so why does the פסוק need 'your elders' and 'your judges'?
steps.simpleTranslation: If he learns from that פסוק, let him learn all of it from there! Why do I need 'your elders' and 'and your judges'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the last answer. If the גזירה שוה works, it should teach the whole law, and then the words in our פסוק would be extra.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גזירה שוה usually brings over the full law from the other place. If 'elders' here is learned from 'elders' there, the words 'your elders' and 'your judges' seem to have nothing left to teach. That cannot be right.

keyTerms.meaning: Let him learn all of it from there

phrases.english: If he learns from it,
let him learn all of it from there!
Why do I need "your elders" and "and your judges"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the גזירה שוה given in step 29.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's use of the גזירה שוה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the גזירה שוה teaches the law, the words of our פסוק become unnecessary.

steps.title: The extra ו is for the count
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops the גזירה שוה. Instead, the extra letter ו in 'and your judges' is what adds to the number of judges for רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the letter ו of 'and your judges' is for the count.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new explanation of רבי יהודה. He does not rely on the גזירה שוה. Instead, the letter ו ('and') in 'and your judges' is what adds to the count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'Rather' shows that the previous explanation is dropped. Now the words 'your elders' and 'your judges' teach that the judges must be the Great סנהדרין. The extra ו is what gives רבי יהודה his higher number.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (the earlier explanation is set aside)

steps.confusionAlert: After the word 'Rather', the גזירה שוה from step 29 is no longer רבי יהודה's source. The extra ו now does the work of adding to the count.

phrases.english: Rather, the vav of "and your judges" is for the count.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by replacing the גזירה שוה with a reading of the letter ו.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Replaces the source: the extra ו is used instead of the גזירה שוה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה learns that they must be the Great סנהדרין from a גזירה שוה.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יהודה reads the extra ו in ״וְשֹׁפְטֶיךָ״ as adding to the number of judges.

steps.title: רבי שמעון does not learn from the ו
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון does not learn anything from an extra ו, so he does not add judges and stays with three.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי שמעון does not learn anything from the letter ו.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the discussion by showing the real root of the disagreement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה learns from an extra ו and רבי שמעון does not. That is why רבי יהודה counts five judges and רבי שמעון counts three.

keyTerms.meaning: He does not learn anything from it

steps.whatToRemember: Both תנאים agree the judges for עגלה ערופה must be the Great סנהדרין. They disagree about the number (five or three) because רבי יהודה learns from the extra ו in ״וְשֹׁפְטֶיךָ״ and רבי שמעון does not.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Shimon does not expound the vav.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why רבי שמעון does not accept the reading in step 31.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The disagreement over five or three judges depends on whether an extra ו teaches anything.

steps.title: Shouldn't the other plural verbs add judges too?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if plural words in the פסוק add judges, then 'they shall go out' and 'they shall measure' should each add two more. That gives nine judges for רבי יהודה and seven for רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if that is so, 'and they shall go out' should add two, and 'and they shall measure' should add two. Then רבי יהודה would have nine judges and רבי שמעון would have seven!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the method it just used. If plural words add judges, the other plural verbs in the same פסוק should add judges too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier steps counted judges from plural words like 'your elders' and 'your judges'. The same פסוק also says 'they shall go out' and 'they shall measure', which are plural as well. Adding two judges for each one makes רבי יהודה's five into nine and רבי שמעון's three into seven. Nobody holds those numbers, so the method seems to prove too much.

keyTerms.meaning: But if that is so: introduces a challenge that takes an idea to its logical end
And they shall go out (a plural verb in the פסוק)
And they shall measure (a plural verb in the פסוק)
Then there would be / here you have

steps.confusionAlert: The numbers nine and seven are nobody's real opinion. The גמרא brings them only to show the problem with counting every plural word.

phrases.english: But now, if that is so,
'And they shall go out' means two,
'And they shall measure' means two,
so according to Rabbi Yehuda there would be nine,
phrases.notes: His five judges plus four more.

phrases.english: and according to Rabbi Shimon, seven?
phrases.notes: His three judges plus four more.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the method of adding judges from plural words, which steps 31 and 32 relied on.
steps.kashyaTarget: The method of counting judges from the plural words in the פסוק
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If plural words add judges, 'they shall go out' and 'they shall measure' must add four more judges. That leads to numbers neither opinion holds.

steps.title: Those verbs are needed for other laws
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that 'they shall go out' and 'they shall measure' are already used for other laws taught in a ברייתא. So they are not free to add judges.
steps.simpleTranslation: That word is needed for what a ברייתא teaches: 'and they shall go out' means they themselves must go, not their messengers. 'And they shall measure' teaches that even if it is found...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The two plural verbs already teach other laws, so they cannot also be used to count judges.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A word that is used for one teaching is not available for another. 'They shall go out' teaches that the judges must come in person and cannot send שלוחים. 'They shall measure' teaches that the measuring must happen even in a special case, and the text stops in the middle of describing that case. Because of this, the count stays at five for רבי יהודה and three for רבי שמעון.

keyTerms.meaning: He needs it: this word is already used for a different teaching
As it was taught in a ברייתא
It is found (the body that was discovered)

steps.whatToRemember: A word in the פסוק that already teaches one law is not free to teach another. That is why 'go out' and 'measure' do not add judges.

phrases.english: That one is needed by him
for that which was taught in a baraita:
'And they shall go out' means they themselves, and not their agents,
'And they shall measure' teaches that even if it is found

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 33.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The word is already used for another teaching
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every plural verb in the פסוק adds two judges, which would give nine or seven.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Go out' and 'measure' teach other laws from a ברייתא: the judges must go in person, and the measuring must be done even in a certain case. So they add no judges.
